requirements.title: Access and workspace state
requirements.rationale: A read must be available to everyone who may see the workspace, on every workspace whose repository is intact, and to nobody else.

criteria.condition: a caller with read access to the workspace, whose credential is an API key, the admin token or a PAT holding `git:read` or `git:write`, calls one of the ten read routes under `/api/v1/workspaces/:slug/scm` on a workspace in status `ready` or `archived`, on a task fork, or on a fork whose parent is `archived`
criteria.action: serve the read from the workspace's repository
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the route's body; the archived workspace and the fork of an archived parent answer the same body they answered before archiving

setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a store in t.TempDir()

workspace `demo` owned by the owner in organization o1, a task fork of it, and a second workspace with its own fork that is archived after the fork was made; all repositories hold one commit on `main`
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/access_test.go, a table over workspace {ready, archived, fork of a ready parent, fork of an archived parent} x credential {owner API key, org member API key, PAT with git:read, PAT with only git:write, admin token}: r = get('/api/v1/workspaces/'+slug+'/scm/refs', cred); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.items is an array; for the ready workspace repeat over the paths of all ten read routes with valid query parameters and assert status 200

criteria.condition: a read route is called without a valid credential, with a PAT that holds neither `git:read` nor `git:write`, or by a caller who has no read access to the workspace
criteria.action: refuse the request without running any git command
criteria.contract: no valid credential: HTTP 401 with `error_type` `unauthenticated`; PAT without the scope: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `insufficient_scope`, for an existing and for a missing workspace alike; no read access: HTTP 404 with `error_type` `not_found`, with a body byte-identical to the one for a slug that does not exist

setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a store in t.TempDir()
workspace `demo` and a user `outsider` who is neither its owner nor a member of its organization; the repository's git runner is wrapped by a recorder
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/access_test.go, a table over the ten read routes: assert get(route, no credential).status == 401 and error_type == 'unauthenticated'; p = PAT with scope changes:read only; assert get(route on 'demo', p).status == 403 and error_type == 'insufficient_scope'; assert get(route on 'nope', p).status == 403; a = get(route on 'demo', outsider key); b = get(route on 'nope', outsider key); assert a.status == 404 and a.error_type == 'not_found' and a.body == b.body; assert the git runner recorded no command

criteria.condition: a read route is called by a caller with read access while the workspace is `pending`, `cloning` or `failed`, has a reclone, archive or delete running, or is a fork whose parent is in `pending`, `cloning` or an archive or delete call
criteria.action: refuse the read without touching the repository
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with `error_type` `workspace_busy` for `pending`, `cloning`, a running reclone, archive or delete, and a fork whose parent is in one of those states; HTTP 409 with `error_type` `workspace_not_ready` for `failed`

setup: the scm routes mounted on an httptest server with a workspace record whose state the test sets
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/access_test.go, a table over the state the precondition of package 10 reports {pending, cloning, reclone running, archive running, delete running, fork with parent cloning -> workspace_busy; failed -> workspace_not_ready}: r = get('/api/v1/workspaces/demo/scm/tree', ownerKey); assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error.error_type == want; assert the git runner recorded no command

criteria.condition: the workspace is a task fork
criteria.action: resolve refs and revisions against the fork's own branches together with the tracking branches at the parent's current heads
criteria.contract: after the parent's `main` moves from c1 to c2, `GET …/scm/refs/main` on the fork answers `sha` c2 with `tracking` true, and `GET …/scm/file?ref=main&path=f.txt` on the fork answers `X-Parley-Resolved-Sha` c2 and the content of c2; a branch created in the fork is listed with `tracking` false and does not appear in the parent's list

setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a store in t.TempDir()
workspace `demo` with `main` at c1 holding f.txt, and a second commit c2 that changes f.txt, present in the repository but not yet on `main`
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/fork_test.go: f = a task fork fixture of 'demo' (a bare repository that borrows demo's objects) served with a ref view (the interface RefView of internal/scm) that lists the fork's own branches and the recorded tracking names at the parent's current heads, as the ref view of package 15 does; push branch 'work' to f; move demo's main from c1 to c2 with a compare-and-swap; r = get(f + '/scm/refs/main'); assert r.json.sha == c2 and r.json.tracking == true; assert get(f + '/scm/file?ref=main&path=f.txt').header('X-Parley-Resolved-Sha') == c2; names = names of get(f + '/scm/refs').json.items; assert 'refs/heads/work' in names with tracking false; assert 'refs/heads/work' not in names of get('demo/scm/refs')

criteria.action: for any request handled by a read route, report exactly one observation to the request recorder, carrying the route's `op` (`refs`, `commits`, `tree`, `file`, `diff`, `compare`, `blame` or `search`) and `result` `ok` when the status is below 400 and `error` otherwise, and emit no hub event
criteria.contract: one recorder call per request: both refs routes report `refs`, both commits routes report `commits`; a 200, a 206 and a 304 report `ok`; a 400, 404, 409, 413 and 503 answered by the read route report `error`

setup: the scm routes mounted on an httptest server with a stub request recorder and a fixture repository
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/recorder_test.go, a table over {refs list, ref get -> 'refs'; commits list, commit get -> 'commits'; tree; file; diff; compare; blame; search} x {a 200 request -> 'ok'; a request with unknown ref -> 'error'}: reset the stub recorder; do the request; assert recorder.calls == [(op, result)]; plus one file request with a matching If-None-Match: assert calls == [('file','ok')]

requirements.title: Revision parameters and consistency
requirements.rationale: Every read names a commit; a caller must be able to say it in the forms git users know and learn exactly which commit answered.

criteria.condition: a read carries a revision parameter (`ref`, `base`, `head`, or `:sha` of the commit route) written as a branch name, a tag name, a full ref name, a full 40-character commit id or an abbreviated commit id of 4 or more hexadecimal characters that matches one commit
criteria.action: resolve it to one commit, peeling an annotated tag to its commit, and name that commit in the response as a full 40-character id
criteria.contract: `resolved_sha` (or `base_sha` and `head_sha`, or `sha` on the commit route) equals the commit's full id; a string starting with `refs/` is taken as a full ref name only

setup: a fixture repository with commits c1..c3 on `main`, branch `feature/x`, lightweight tag `v1`, annotated tag `v2` and the ref `refs/parley/changes/12/3`, served as workspace `demo`
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/revision_test.go, a table over ref = {'main', 'feature/x', 'v1' (lightweight tag), 'v2' (annotated tag), 'refs/heads/main', 'refs/tags/v2', 'refs/parley/changes/12/3', full id of c2, first 7 characters of c2}: r = get('/scm/tree?ref=' + urlencode(ref)); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.resolved_sha == want and len(want) == 40; d = get('/scm/diff?base=v1&head=feature/x'); assert d.json.base_sha == id(v1) and d.json.head_sha == id(feature/x); c = get('/scm/commits/feature%2Fx'); assert c.json.sha == id(feature/x)

criteria.condition: a read route whose `ref` parameter is optional is called without it
criteria.action: use the head of the workspace's default branch
criteria.contract: the response's `resolved_sha` equals the current head of the default branch

setup: a fixture repository whose default branch is `trunk`, with a second branch `main` at another commit
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/revision_test.go, a table over the routes {commits, tree, file?path=f.txt, blame?path=f.txt, search?q=x} on a workspace whose default branch is 'trunk': assert response.resolved_sha (X-Parley-Resolved-Sha for the raw file) == head('trunk')

criteria.condition: a revision parameter names nothing in the repository, is the name of both a branch and a tag, is an abbreviated id that matches more than one commit, names an object that is not a commit, or is an expression other than the five accepted forms (for example `main~2`, `HEAD`, `@{1}`, a string starting with `-`)
criteria.action: refuse the read
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with `error_type` `ref_not_found`; no part of the string reaches the `git` command line as an option

setup: the fixture of the resolution test plus a branch and a tag both named `dup`, and two commits created so that their ids share the first 4 characters
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/revision_test.go, a table over ref = {'nope', 'dup' (branch and tag of that name), a 4-character prefix shared by two commits, the id of a blob, 'main~2', 'HEAD', '@{1}', '--all', 'refs/heads/nope'}: r = get('/scm/tree?ref=' + urlencode(ref)); assert r.status == 404 and r.json.error.error_type == 'ref_not_found'; the same table against /scm/commits/{ref} and /scm/diff?base={ref}&head=main

criteria.condition: a read names, by full 40-character id, a commit that is reachable from no ref while its object is still in the repository
criteria.action: serve the read from that commit
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `resolved_sha` equal to the id

setup: a fixture repository with a branch `gone` whose head commit is on no other ref
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/revision_test.go: c = head of branch 'gone'; delete refs/heads/gone in the fixture; r = get('/scm/file?ref=' + c + '&path=only-on-gone.txt'); assert r.status == 200 and r.body == the file's bytes; assert get('/scm/commits/' + c).json.sha == c

criteria.action: for any read request, resolve each revision parameter exactly once and compute the whole response from the resolved commit ids, so that a read that runs while the named ref is moved from an old to a new commit answers for the old or for the new commit
criteria.contract: every response obtained during concurrent moves of the ref has status 200, a `resolved_sha` equal to one of the two commits and content equal to that commit's content

setup: a fixture repository in which f.txt differs between commits c1 and c2, c2 a child of c1
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/consistency_test.go: start a goroutine that moves refs/heads/main between c1 and c2 with compare-and-swap until stopped; 200 times: r = get('/scm/file?ref=main&path=f.txt'); assert r.status == 200; s = r.header('X-Parley-Resolved-Sha'); assert s in {c1, c2}; assert r.body == content of f.txt at s; the same loop for /scm/tree?ref=main&recursive=true asserting tree_sha == tree of resolved_sha

requirements.title: Caching headers, read timeout and limits
requirements.rationale: Answers addressed by commit id never change, so they should be cacheable forever; every other read should be cheap to revalidate, and no read may run without bound.

criteria.condition: a read on the commits, commit, tree, file, diff, compare, blame or search route succeeds and every revision parameter of the request was given as a 40-character commit id
criteria.action: mark the response immutable
criteria.contract: the response carries `Cache-Control: private, max-age=31536000, immutable` and a non-empty quoted `ETag`

setup: the scm routes on an httptest server with a fixture repository of two commits
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/cache_test.go, a table over {commits?ref=C, commits/C, tree?ref=C, file?ref=C&path=f.txt, diff?base=C1&head=C, compare?base=C1&head=C, blame?ref=C&path=f.txt, search?ref=C&q=x} with C and C1 full ids: r = get(route); assert r.header('Cache-Control') == 'private, max-age=31536000, immutable'; assert r.header('ETag') matches a quoted string; and diff?base=main&head=C is not immutable

criteria.condition: any other read succeeds: a revision given as a name or an abbreviated id, an omitted `ref`, or one of the two refs routes
criteria.action: answer with a revalidation tag derived from the resolved commit ids, the query and the representation
criteria.contract: the response carries `Cache-Control: private, no-cache` and an `ETag` that is equal for two identical requests while no named ref moves, differs after a named ref moves, and differs between the raw and the JSON form of the file route, which also carries `Vary: Accept`

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/cache_test.go: a = get('/scm/file?ref=main&path=f.txt'); b = same; assert a.header('Cache-Control') == 'private, no-cache' and a.header('ETag') == b.header('ETag'); j = same with Accept: application/json; assert j.header('ETag') != a.header('ETag') and a.header('Vary') contains 'Accept'; move main to c2; c = get(same); assert c.header('ETag') != a.header('ETag'); l1 = get('/scm/refs'); create branch x; l2 = get('/scm/refs'); assert l1.header('ETag') != l2.header('ETag'); assert get('/scm/tree').header('Cache-Control') == 'private, no-cache'

criteria.condition: a read arrives with an `If-None-Match` header that contains the `ETag` the response would carry, alone or in a comma-separated list
criteria.action: answer that the caller's copy is current, without a body
criteria.contract: HTTP 304 with an empty body and the same `ETag` and `Cache-Control` headers a 200 would carry; a header that does not contain the tag gets the full 200 response

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/cache_test.go, a table over {file by name, file by full id, refs list, diff by names}: e = get(route).header('ETag'); r = get(route, If-None-Match: e); assert r.status == 304 and len(r.body) == 0 and r.header('ETag') == e; r2 = get(route, If-None-Match: '"other", ' + e); assert r2.status == 304; r3 = get(route, If-None-Match: '"other"'); assert r3.status == 200; move main; assert get(file by name, If-None-Match: e).status == 200

criteria.condition: a read has not finished when `[scm].read_timeout` (default 30 s) has passed since the read route began handling it
criteria.action: end the read's `git` subprocess and answer that the read timed out
criteria.contract: HTTP 503 with `error_type` `scm_timeout`; the subprocess's context is cancelled and no `git` process of the request is left running

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/timeout_test.go, a table over {tree, file, diff, compare, blame, search}: configure read_timeout = 50ms and a git runner stub that blocks until its context is done and records the cancellation; t0 = now; r = get(route); assert r.status == 503 and r.json.error.error_type == 'scm_timeout'; assert now - t0 < 2s; assert stub.cancelled == true; and in internal/gitrepo/read_test.go: run a real `git` command through the runner with a context that is cancelled; assert the call returns the context error and the process has exited

criteria.condition: the configuration sets `[scm].read_timeout` or `[scm].max_file_size`
criteria.action: use the configured values in place of the defaults of 30 s and 32 MiB
criteria.contract: with `max_file_size = "1KB"` a 2,000-byte file answers 413 and a 500-byte file answers 200; with no `[scm]` section the loaded values are 30 s and 33,554,432 bytes

check.pseudocode: in internal/config/scm_test.go: cfg = load(''); assert cfg.SCM.ReadTimeout == 30s and cfg.SCM.MaxFileSize == 32 << 20; cfg = load('[scm]\nread_timeout = "5s"\nmax_file_size = "1KB"'); assert cfg.SCM.ReadTimeout == 5s; and in internal/scm/file_test.go: with the limit taken from that configuration, get(file of 2000 bytes).status == 413 and get(file of 500 bytes).status == 200

criteria.condition: the configuration sets `[scm].read_timeout` or `[scm].max_file_size` to zero or to a negative value
criteria.action: refuse to start
criteria.contract: configuration loading returns an error whose message names the key; `parleyd` exits with a non-zero status without opening its listener

check.pseudocode: in internal/config/scm_test.go, a table over {read_timeout = "0s", read_timeout = "-1s", max_file_size = "0"}: _, err = load(text); assert err != nil and err.Error() contains the key name '[scm].read_timeout' or '[scm].max_file_size'

requirements.title: Refs
requirements.rationale: Listing and reading refs is how a client without a clone finds the commits to read.

criteria.condition: a caller requests `GET …/scm/refs`, with or without `prefix`, `limit` and `cursor`
criteria.action: list the refs under `refs/heads/`, `refs/tags/` and `refs/parley/` whose full name starts with `prefix` (default `refs/heads/`) as ref objects in ascending byte order of name, paged
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `{items, next_cursor}`; a prefix that matches no ref answers `items: []` and `next_cursor: null`; following `next_cursor` to the end returns every matching ref exactly once; refs in other namespaces (for example `refs/notes/x`) never appear

setup: a fixture repository with five branches (one named `feature/x`), tags `v1` and `v2`, `refs/parley/changes/12/3` and `refs/notes/x`
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/refs_test.go: r = get('/scm/refs'); assert names(r) == sorted names of all branches; assert names(get('/scm/refs?prefix=refs/tags/')) == ['refs/tags/v1','refs/tags/v2']; assert names(get('/scm/refs?prefix=refs/parley/changes/')) == ['refs/parley/changes/12/3']; assert names(get('/scm/refs?prefix=refs/heads/feature/')) == ['refs/heads/feature/x']; assert get('/scm/refs?prefix=refs/none/').json == {items: [], next_cursor: null}; assert 'refs/notes/x' not in names(get('/scm/refs?prefix=refs/')); page with limit=2 until next_cursor is null; assert the concatenation == the unpaged list

criteria.action: for any ref object returned, set `name` to the full ref name, `kind` to `branch`, `tag` or `hub` by namespace, `sha` to the full id of the commit the ref points at (the peeled commit for an annotated tag), `protected` to true for a branch in the workspace's protected branches and for every `refs/parley/` ref, `tracking` to true for a fork's tracking branch, and `change` to `{workspace_slug, number}` when the change lookup names an open or draft change whose source is the branch, else null
criteria.contract: each ref object has exactly the six members `name`, `kind`, `sha`, `protected`, `tracking`, `change`; with the default lookups only the default branch and hub-owned refs are protected and `change` is null

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/refs_test.go, a table over {refs/heads/main -> kind branch, protected true; refs/heads/feature/x -> branch, protected false; refs/tags/v2 -> tag, sha == commit the annotated tag peels to, protected false; refs/parley/changes/12/3 -> hub, protected true}: o = get('/scm/refs/' + name).json; assert keys(o) == {name, kind, sha, protected, tracking, change}; assert the row's values; assert o.tracking == false and o.change == null; then with stub lookups (protected = ['feature/x'], change of feature/x = {demo, 12}): assert get('/scm/refs/feature/x').json.protected == true and .change == {workspace_slug: 'demo', number: 12}

criteria.condition: a caller requests `GET …/scm/refs/*name` with a full ref name, or with a branch name that does not start with `refs/`
criteria.action: return that ref's object, reading a name without the `refs/` start as `refs/heads/<name>`
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the ref object; `…/refs/feature/x` and `…/refs/refs/heads/feature/x` answer the same object

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/refs_test.go: a = get('/scm/refs/feature/x'); b = get('/scm/refs/refs/heads/feature/x'); assert a.status == 200 and a.json == b.json and a.json.name == 'refs/heads/feature/x'; assert get('/scm/refs/refs/tags/v1').json.kind == 'tag'

criteria.condition: `GET …/scm/refs/*name` names a ref that does not exist, or a ref outside `refs/heads/`, `refs/tags/` and `refs/parley/`
criteria.action: refuse the read
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with `error_type` `ref_not_found`

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/refs_test.go, a table over name = {'nope', 'refs/heads/nope', 'v1' (a tag, not a branch), 'refs/notes/x'}: r = get('/scm/refs/' + name); assert r.status == 404 and r.json.error.error_type == 'ref_not_found'

requirements.title: Commits
requirements.rationale: History, of a ref or of one path, answers who changed what and under which change, without a checkout.

criteria.condition: a caller requests `GET …/scm/commits`
criteria.action: list the commits reachable from `ref`, newest first, following first parents only unless `first_parent=false`, paged, and name the resolved commit
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `{items, next_cursor, resolved_sha}`; with `first_parent` absent the commits of a merged side branch are not listed and with `first_parent=false` they are; all pages of one listing come from the commit the first page resolved, also when the ref moves between pages

setup: a fixture repository whose `main` is c1 <- c2 <- m, where m merges a side branch holding commit s1
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/commits_test.go: r = get('/scm/commits?ref=main'); assert shas(r) == [m, c2, c1] (merge m, then its first-parent line) and r.json.resolved_sha == m; assert s1 (side-branch commit) not in shas(r); assert s1 in shas(get('/scm/commits?ref=main&first_parent=false')); p1 = get('/scm/commits?ref=main&limit=2'); move main to a new commit; p2 = get('/scm/commits?ref=main&limit=2&cursor=' + p1.json.next_cursor); assert shas(p1) + shas(p2) == [m, c2, c1] and p2.json.resolved_sha == m and p2.json.next_cursor == null

criteria.condition: a commit listing carries `path`, `follow`, `since`, `until` or `author`
criteria.action: return only the commits that changed `path` (across renames of that single file when `follow=true`), whose committer time is at or after `since` and at or before `until`, and whose author name or e-mail contains `author` without regard to case
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the filtered list; a `path` that no commit changed answers `items: []`

setup: a fixture repository with commits by two authors at fixed committer times T1 < T2 < T3, a file renamed from old.md to new.md, and a directory docs/
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/commits_test.go, a table over query -> expected shas: {path=docs/a.md -> commits that changed it; path=docs (a directory) -> commits that changed anything below it; path=new.md -> [rename commit]; path=new.md&follow=true -> [rename commit, commits that changed old.md]; since=T2 -> commits with committer time >= T2; until=T1 -> commits with committer time <= T1; author=ALICE -> commits of 'Alice <alice@example.com>'; author=example.org -> commits of bob@example.org; path=never.txt -> []}

criteria.action: for any commit object returned by a read route, set `sha`, `parents` and `tree_sha` to full ids, `author` and `committer` to `{name, email, time}` with `time` as an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp, `message` to the full commit message, `change` to `{workspace_slug, number, version}` when the change lookup knows the commit as a version head or as landed by a change and null otherwise, and `session_id` to the session the session lookup names or null; and include `stats` (`{files_changed, insertions, deletions}`) on a list only when `stats=true`
criteria.contract: a listed commit without `stats=true` has no `stats` member; with it, `stats` equals the commit's numbers against its first parent; with the default lookups `change` and `session_id` are null

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/commits_test.go: o = get('/scm/commits?ref=main').json.items[1]; assert o.sha == c2 and o.parents == [c1] and o.tree_sha == tree(c2); assert o.author == {name: 'Alice', email: 'alice@example.com', time: '2026-01-02T03:04:05Z'}; assert o.message == the full multi-line message; assert 'stats' not in o and o.change == null and o.session_id == null; s = get('/scm/commits?ref=main&stats=true').json.items[1].stats; assert s == {files_changed: 2, insertions: 5, deletions: 1}; with stub lookups (c2 -> change {demo, 12, 3}, session 'sess-1'): assert o.change == {workspace_slug: 'demo', number: 12, version: 3} and o.session_id == 'sess-1'

criteria.condition: a caller requests `GET …/scm/commits/:sha` with any revision in `:sha`
criteria.action: return that commit's object with `stats`, and with `files=true` also `files`, the file changes against the commit's first parent, or against the empty tree for a commit without a parent
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the commit object including `stats`; `files` is absent unless `files=true`; each entry of `files` is a file change `{path, old_path, status, insertions, deletions, binary, old_sha, new_sha}`

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/commits_test.go: r = get('/scm/commits/' + c2); assert r.json.sha == c2 and r.json.stats.files_changed == 2 and 'files' not in r.json; f = get('/scm/commits/main?files=true'); assert f.json.files is the changes of m against its first parent c2; root = get('/scm/commits/' + c1 + '?files=true'); assert every root.json.files[i].status == 'added'; assert get('/scm/commits/feature%2Fx').status == 200

criteria.condition: a commits request carries a boolean parameter (`follow`, `first_parent`, `stats`, `files`) that is neither `true` nor `false`, a `since` or `until` that is not an RFC 3339 timestamp, or `follow=true` without `path`
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/commits_test.go, a table over {commits?stats=yes, commits?first_parent=1, commits?since=yesterday, commits?until=2026-13-01T00:00:00Z, commits?follow=true, commits/main?files=maybe}: r = get(route); assert r.status == 400 and r.json.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'

requirements.title: Tree and file
requirements.rationale: One directory listing or one file at a ref is the smallest useful read; it must cost one request.

criteria.condition: a caller requests `GET …/scm/tree`
criteria.action: list the entries of the directory `path` (default: the root) at `ref`, ordered by `path` in ascending byte order, as tree entries `{path, name, type, mode, sha, size}`, with `resolved_sha` and the listed directory's `tree_sha`
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `{items, next_cursor, resolved_sha, tree_sha}`; `type` is `blob`, `tree`, `commit` for a submodule entry or `symlink`; `mode` is git's six-digit octal string; `size` is present only on entries of type `blob`

setup: a fixture repository whose `main` holds README.md, an executable run.sh, a symlink `link`, a directory docs/ with a.md and api/b.md, and a submodule entry at vendor/sub
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/tree_test.go: r = get('/scm/tree?ref=main'); assert paths(r) == sorted root entries and r.json.tree_sha == tree(main) and r.json.resolved_sha == head(main); by type: assert entry('README.md') == {path: 'README.md', name: 'README.md', type: 'blob', mode: '100644', sha: blob id, size: byte length}; assert entry('run.sh').mode == '100755'; assert entry('docs').type == 'tree' and 'size' not in entry('docs'); assert entry('link').type == 'symlink' and entry('link').mode == '120000'; assert entry('vendor/sub').type == 'commit' via get('/scm/tree?path=vendor'); d = get('/scm/tree?ref=main&path=docs'); assert d.json.items[0].path == 'docs/a.md' and d.json.items[0].name == 'a.md' and d.json.tree_sha == tree id of docs

criteria.condition: a tree request carries `recursive=true`, `limit` or `cursor`
criteria.action: with `recursive=true` list every entry below `path`, directories and their contents alike; return at most `limit` entries per page, where `limit` defaults to 1,000 and may be 1 to 10,000
criteria.contract: the recursive listing of the fixture contains `docs`, `docs/a.md`, `docs/api` and `docs/api/b.md` in that order; a listing of 1,500 entries answers 1,000 entries and a non-null `next_cursor`, and the second page answers the remaining 500 with `next_cursor: null`; `limit=10000` is accepted

setup: the tree fixture plus a branch `big` whose root holds 1,500 files, created with `git fast-import`
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/tree_test.go: r = get('/scm/tree?ref=main&recursive=true'); assert ['docs','docs/a.md','docs/api','docs/api/b.md'] is a contiguous run of paths(r); big = get('/scm/tree?ref=big'); assert len(big.json.items) == 1000 and big.json.next_cursor != null; p2 = get('/scm/tree?ref=big&cursor=' + big.json.next_cursor); assert len(p2.json.items) == 500 and p2.json.next_cursor == null and no path repeats; assert get('/scm/tree?ref=big&limit=10000').status == 200 and len(items) == 1500

criteria.condition: a tree request names a `path` that does not exist at the commit, a `path` that is a file, a `path` that is not a legal repository path (an empty segment, a leading `/`, a `.` or `..` segment, or anything under `.git`), or a `limit` outside 1 to 10,000
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with `error_type` `path_not_found` for a path that does not exist; HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request` for a file, an illegal path and a `limit` out of bounds

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/tree_test.go, a table: {path=nope -> 404 path_not_found; path=docs/nope -> 404 path_not_found; path=README.md -> 400 invalid_request; path=/docs, path=docs//api, path=docs/../x, path=./docs, path=.git/config -> 400 invalid_request; limit=0, limit=10001, limit=x -> 400 invalid_request}: r = get('/scm/tree?ref=main&' + q); assert (r.status, r.json.error.error_type) == want

criteria.condition: a caller requests `GET …/scm/file` with `path` naming a file or a symlink, without `Accept: application/json`
criteria.action: return the file's bytes, or the link target as text for a symlink
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the exact bytes as body, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, `Content-Length`, `X-Parley-Blob-Sha` (the blob id), `X-Parley-Resolved-Sha` (the commit's full id) and `X-Parley-File-Mode` (`100644`, `100755` or `120000`)

setup: the tree fixture plus bin.dat and empty.txt on `main`
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/file_test.go, a table over path = {README.md (text, 100644), run.sh (100755), bin.dat (bytes 0x00..0xff), empty.txt (0 bytes), link (symlink to README.md)}: r = get('/scm/file?ref=main&path=' + path); assert r.status == 200 and r.body == git cat-file bytes (for link: 'README.md'); assert r.header('Content-Type') == 'application/octet-stream'; assert r.header('X-Parley-Blob-Sha') == blob id and r.header('X-Parley-Resolved-Sha') == head(main) and r.header('X-Parley-File-Mode') == mode

criteria.condition: a raw file request carries a `Range` header with exactly one byte range that starts inside the file
criteria.action: return only that part of the file
criteria.contract: HTTP 206 with the bytes of the range, `Content-Range: bytes <first>-<last>/<size>` and the same `X-Parley-*` headers; the forms `bytes=a-b`, `bytes=a-` and `bytes=-n` are honoured and an end past the file is cut to its last byte; a header with several ranges, and any `Range` on a request with `Accept: application/json`, gets the whole file with HTTP 200

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/file_test.go, on a 100-byte file, a table: {'bytes=0-9' -> 206, body[0:10], 'bytes 0-9/100'; 'bytes=90-' -> 206, body[90:100], 'bytes 90-99/100'; 'bytes=-5' -> 206, body[95:100]; 'bytes=50-500' -> 206, 'bytes 50-99/100'; 'bytes=0-1,5-6' -> 200 whole file}: r = get(file, Range: h); assert status, body and Content-Range; r = get(file, Range: 'bytes=0-9', Accept: 'application/json'); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.size == 100

criteria.condition: a file request carries `Accept: application/json`
criteria.action: return the file as a JSON object whose `content` is the text when the bytes are valid UTF-8 and their base64 encoding otherwise
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `{path, sha, mode, size, encoding, content, resolved_sha}`: `sha` is the blob id, `size` the byte length, `encoding` is `utf8` or `base64`, and decoding `content` by `encoding` gives the file's exact bytes

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/file_test.go, a table over {README.md -> utf8; a file with multi-byte UTF-8 text -> utf8; bin.dat -> base64; empty.txt -> utf8 with content ''}: r = get('/scm/file?ref=main&path=' + p, Accept: 'application/json'); assert r.header('Content-Type') starts with 'application/json'; assert keys(r.json) == {path, sha, mode, size, encoding, content, resolved_sha}; assert r.json.encoding == want; assert decode(r.json.content, r.json.encoding) == file bytes; assert r.json.size == len(file bytes) and r.json.mode == '100644'

criteria.condition: a file request has no `path`, names a path that does not exist at the commit, names a directory or a submodule entry, names an illegal repository path, or carries a single `Range` that starts at or after the end of the file
criteria.action: refuse the request and send no file content
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request` for a missing `path`, a directory, a submodule entry and an illegal path; HTTP 404 with `error_type` `path_not_found` for a path that does not exist; HTTP 416 with `error_type` `range_not_satisfiable` and `Content-Range: bytes */<size>` for the range; in the raw and the JSON form alike the body is the JSON error envelope

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/file_test.go, a table: {no path -> 400 invalid_request; path=docs -> 400 invalid_request; path=vendor/sub -> 400 invalid_request; path=../x -> 400 invalid_request; path=nope.txt -> 404 path_not_found; path=README.md with Range 'bytes=99999-' -> 416 range_not_satisfiable}: for accept in {none, 'application/json'} (the range row raw only): r = get(route); assert (r.status, r.json.error.error_type) == want and r.json.error.code == r.status

criteria.condition: the file named by a file request is larger than `[scm].max_file_size` (default 32 MiB)
criteria.action: refuse the read without sending content, for whole-file and ranged requests alike
criteria.contract: HTTP 413 with `error_type` `payload_too_large` and the member `size` (the file's size in bytes) inside `error`; a file of exactly the limit is served with HTTP 200

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/file_test.go, with max_file_size configured to 1024: big = file of 1025 bytes, edge = file of 1024 bytes; for accept in {none, 'application/json'}: r = get(big); assert r.status == 413 and r.json.error.error_type == 'payload_too_large' and r.json.error.size == 1025; assert get(big, Range: 'bytes=0-9').status == 413; assert get(edge).status == 200 and len(body) == 1024

requirements.title: Diff and compare
requirements.rationale: A reviewer needs what a head adds as data, and whether it would still apply, without fetching either side.

criteria.condition: a caller requests `GET …/scm/diff` with `base` and `head`
criteria.action: compare the merge base of `base` and `head` with `head` when `mode` is absent or `merge_base`, and `base` itself with `head` when `mode=direct`, and return the result as JSON
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `{base_sha, head_sha, merge_base_sha, files, stats, truncated}`: in `merge_base` mode a file changed only on `base` since the merge base is not in `files`, in `direct` mode it is; `merge_base_sha` is the merge base's full id in both modes, or null when the two commits share no ancestor, in which case the left side in `merge_base` mode is the empty tree; `stats` is `{files_changed, insertions, deletions}` over the whole diff

setup: a fixture repository in which `main` and `feature` diverge from commit mb: `main` adds only-main.txt, `feature` changes several files; and a branch `orphan` with no common ancestor
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/diff_test.go: r = get('/scm/diff?base=main&head=feature'); assert r.json.base_sha == head(main) and r.json.head_sha == head(feature) and r.json.merge_base_sha == mb; assert paths(r) == files changed on feature since mb and 'only-main.txt' not in paths(r); assert r.json.truncated == false and r.json.stats.files_changed == len(r.json.files); d = get('/scm/diff?base=main&head=feature&mode=direct'); assert 'only-main.txt' in paths(d) and d.json.merge_base_sha == mb; o = get('/scm/diff?base=main&head=orphan'); assert o.json.merge_base_sha == null and every file of orphan has status 'added'

criteria.action: for any file change returned by diff, compare or a commit read, set `path`, `status` (`added`, `modified`, `deleted`, `renamed`, `copied` or `type_changed`, with rename detection on), `old_path` (the previous path for `renamed` and `copied`, null otherwise), `insertions` and `deletions` (line counts, 0 for a binary file), `binary`, and `old_sha` and `new_sha` (blob ids, null on the side where the file does not exist); on the diff route with patches on, add `patch`, the file's unified diff text, except for binary files
criteria.contract: a file moved with small edits is one entry with `status` `renamed` and both paths, not a deletion and an addition; a file whose mode changes from regular file to symlink is `type_changed`; files are ordered by `path`

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/diff_test.go, on base = c1 and head = c2 of a fixture built for the table: f = files of get('/scm/diff?base=' + c1 + '&head=' + c2) by path; assert f['new.txt'].status == 'added' and old_sha == null and insertions == 3; assert f['gone.txt'].status == 'deleted' and new_sha == null; assert f['edit.txt'] == {status: 'modified', insertions: 2, deletions: 1, binary: false, old_path: null, ...} and f['edit.txt'].patch contains '@@'; assert f['moved/b.txt'].status == 'renamed' and old_path == 'a.txt' and 'a.txt' not in f; assert f['img.bin'].binary == true and insertions == 0 and 'patch' not in f['img.bin']; assert f['kind'].status == 'type_changed'; assert paths are sorted

criteria.condition: a diff request carries `path`, `patches`, `context` or `format`
criteria.action: keep only the files whose path matches at least one `path` glob (`*` within one segment, `**` across segments), omit `patch` when `patches=false`, use `context` lines of context (default 3) in patch text, and with `format=patch` answer the unified diff as text
criteria.contract: with `path=docs/**` only files under `docs/` are in `files` and in `stats`; with `patches=false` no file has a `patch` member; with `context=0` a one-line edit's patch has no context lines; with `format=patch` the response is HTTP 200 with `Content-Type: text/x-diff` and a body that `git apply --check` accepts on the left side's tree

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/diff_test.go: r = get(diff + '&path=docs/**&path=*.md'); assert every path matches one of the globs and r.json.stats.files_changed == len(files); assert no file in get(diff + '&patches=false').json.files has 'patch'; p0 = patch of edit.txt from get(diff + '&context=0'); assert p0 has no line starting with ' '; p20 = get(diff + '&context=20'); assert p20.status == 200; t = get(diff + '&format=patch'); assert t.header('Content-Type') starts with 'text/x-diff'; check out the merge base in a temp work tree and assert `git apply --check` of t.body exits 0

criteria.condition: the diff to return holds more than 5,000 files or more than 8 MiB of patch text
criteria.action: return the first 5,000 files in path order, add patch text file by file until the next file's patch would take the total past 8 MiB, return the later files without `patch`, and say that the result is cut
criteria.contract: `truncated` is true; `files` has at most 5,000 entries; the sum of the lengths of all `patch` members is at most 8,388,608 bytes; `stats` still counts the whole diff; with `format=patch` the text ends at a file boundary within the same limits and the response carries `X-Parley-Truncated: true`

setup: a branch `many` adding 5,001 one-line files and a branch `wide` adding three text files of 3 MiB each, both created with `git fast-import` on top of an empty root commit `empty`
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/diff_test.go: r = get('/scm/diff?base=' + empty + '&head=many'); assert len(r.json.files) == 5000 and r.json.truncated == true and r.json.stats.files_changed == 5001; w = get('/scm/diff?base=' + empty + '&head=wide'); assert w.json.truncated == true and len(w.json.files) == 3 and sum(len(f.patch) for files with patch) <= 8 << 20 and exactly the last file has no patch; t = get(same + '&format=patch'); assert t.header('X-Parley-Truncated') == 'true' and len(t.body) <= 8 << 20; small = get(diff of the ordinary fixture); assert small.json.truncated == false

criteria.condition: a diff or compare request lacks `base` or `head`, or a diff request carries a `mode` other than `merge_base` and `direct`, a `format` other than `json` and `patch`, a `context` that is not an integer from 0 to 20, or a `patches` value that is neither `true` nor `false`
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/diff_test.go, a table over {diff?head=main, diff?base=main, compare?base=main, compare?head=main, diff?base=a&head=b&mode=three_dot, &format=html, &context=21, &context=-1, &context=x, &patches=no}: r = get(route); assert r.status == 400 and r.json.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'

criteria.condition: a caller requests `GET …/scm/compare` with `base` and `head`, and every commit of `head` that is not in `base` applies on top of `base` in a trial rebase
criteria.action: report how the two commits relate and that the rebase would succeed, without moving any ref
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `{base_sha, head_sha, merge_base_sha, ahead, behind, commits, files, mergeable: "clean", conflict: null}`: `ahead` and `behind` count the commits only in `head` and only in `base`; `commits` holds at most 200 commit objects of `head` not in `base`, oldest first, without `stats`; `files` holds at most 5,000 file changes from the merge base to `head` without `patch`; a `head` contained in `base` answers `ahead: 0`, `commits: []`, `files: []` and `clean`

setup: a fixture repository in which `feature` (commits f1, f2) and `main` (one commit) diverge from mb and touch different files, and a branch `long` with 250 commits on top of mb
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/compare_test.go: before = all refs with ids; r = get('/scm/compare?base=main&head=feature'); assert r.json.ahead == 2 and r.json.behind == 1 and r.json.merge_base_sha == mb; assert shas(r.json.commits) == [f1, f2] and 'stats' not in r.json.commits[0]; assert paths(r.json.files) == files changed by f1 and f2; assert r.json.mergeable == 'clean' and r.json.conflict == null; assert all refs with ids == before; s = get('/scm/compare?base=main&head=' + mb); assert s.json.ahead == 0 and s.json.commits == [] and s.json.mergeable == 'clean'; l = get('/scm/compare?base=main&head=long'); assert l.json.ahead == 250 and len(l.json.commits) == 200 and l.json.commits[0].sha == oldest commit of long not in main

criteria.condition: a compare request's trial rebase stops because a commit of `head` does not apply on top of `base`
criteria.action: report the conflict as data, without moving any ref
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `mergeable: "conflict"` and `conflict` set to a conflict report: `target_sha` (= `base_sha`), `head_sha`, `base_sha` (the merge base), `commit_sha` (the first commit that did not apply), `files` with one entry per conflicted file `{path, kind, base, ours, theirs, landed_by: []}` where each side is `{sha, mode, path}` or null, `landed_changes: []` and `change: null`; `kind` is `content` when both sides edited the same lines, `add_add` when both added the path, `modify_delete` when the target changed a file the head deleted and `delete_modify` for the reverse

setup: a fixture repository with `main` and four branches that each conflict with it on f.txt in one of the four ways
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/compare_test.go, a table over head = {both-edit (content), both-add (add_add), head-deletes (modify_delete), base-deletes (delete_modify)}: before = all refs with ids; r = get('/scm/compare?base=main&head=' + head); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.mergeable == 'conflict'; c = r.json.conflict; assert c.target_sha == r.json.base_sha and c.head_sha == r.json.head_sha and c.base_sha == r.json.merge_base_sha; assert c.commit_sha == the conflicting commit of head (the second of two for 'both-edit', whose first commit applies); assert c.files == [{path: 'f.txt', kind: want, base: ..., ours: ..., theirs: ..., landed_by: []}] with null on the side where the file does not exist and ours.sha == blob of f.txt on main; assert c.landed_changes == [] and c.change == null; assert all refs with ids == before; and in internal/gitrepo/trial_test.go the same table against the trial rebase function directly

criteria.condition: the commits of `head` that are not in `base` in a compare request include a merge commit
criteria.action: refuse the comparison
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `merge_commits_unsupported`

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/compare_test.go: r = get('/scm/compare?base=old&head=main') where main holds merge commit m after old; assert r.status == 400 and r.json.error.error_type == 'merge_commits_unsupported'; assert get('/scm/diff?base=old&head=main').status == 200 (diff has no such limit)

requirements.title: Blame
requirements.rationale: Tools answer "who changed this and in which change" from the hub when blame names commits and changes.

criteria.condition: a caller requests `GET …/scm/blame` with `path` naming a text file of at most 2 MiB
criteria.action: return, for the whole file, the ranges of adjacent lines that were last changed by the same commit at adjacent original lines
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `{resolved_sha, path, ranges}`; each range is `{start_line, end_line, commit, original_path, original_start_line}` with 1-based inclusive lines; the ranges are in line order, do not overlap and cover lines 1 to the last line; an empty file answers `ranges: []`

setup: a fixture repository in which f.txt has six lines: 1-2 from c1, 4-6 from c2, line 3 from c3; and an empty file empty.txt
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/blame_test.go: r = get('/scm/blame?ref=main&path=f.txt'); assert r.json.resolved_sha == head(main) and r.json.path == 'f.txt'; assert [(x.start_line, x.end_line, x.commit.sha) for x in ranges] == [(1,2,c1),(3,3,c3),(4,6,c2)]; assert ranges[0].original_path == 'f.txt' and ranges[0].original_start_line == 1; assert get('/scm/blame?path=empty.txt').json.ranges == []; and in internal/gitrepo/blame_test.go the same expectation against the blame function

criteria.condition: a blame request carries `start_line`, `end_line` or both
criteria.action: return only the ranges inside lines `start_line` (default 1) to `end_line` (default: the last line), cutting ranges at the boundaries and cutting an `end_line` past the last line to it
criteria.contract: HTTP 200; with `start_line=2&end_line=4` on the fixture the ranges are lines 2-2, 3-3 and 4-4; with `end_line=999` the last range ends at the file's last line

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/blame_test.go: r = get('/scm/blame?path=f.txt&start_line=2&end_line=4'); assert [(x.start_line, x.end_line, x.commit.sha)] == [(2,2,c1),(3,3,c3),(4,4,c2)]; assert ranges[0].original_start_line == 2; e = get('/scm/blame?path=f.txt&start_line=5&end_line=999'); assert e.json.ranges == [range 5-6 of c2]; assert get('/scm/blame?path=f.txt&start_line=6').json.ranges[0].end_line == 6

criteria.action: for any blame range, set `commit` to the commit object of the commit that last changed the lines, without `stats` and with `change` and `session_id` from the lookups, and set `original_path` and `original_start_line` to the file's path and the range's first line in that commit, following renames of the file
criteria.contract: lines last changed before the file was renamed carry the old path in `original_path`; no range's `commit` has a `stats` member; with a change lookup that knows the commit, `commit.change` is `{workspace_slug, number, version}`

setup: the blame fixture plus a file written as before.txt and later renamed to renamed.txt with one more line added
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/blame_test.go: r = get('/scm/blame?path=renamed.txt'); x = the range from the commit before the rename; assert x.original_path == 'before.txt' and x.commit.sha == that commit; assert 'stats' not in x.commit and x.commit.message != ''; with a stub change lookup (c2 -> {demo, 12, 3}): assert the range of c2 in f.txt has commit.change == {workspace_slug: 'demo', number: 12, version: 3}

criteria.condition: a blame request has no `path`, names a path that does not exist at the commit, a directory or a submodule entry, a binary file, a file larger than 2 MiB (2,097,152 bytes), or a line range in which `start_line` is below 1, above `end_line` or past the file's last line, or a value is not an integer
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with `error_type` `path_not_found` for a path that does not exist; HTTP 413 with `error_type` `payload_too_large` for a file over 2 MiB, while a file of exactly 2 MiB is served; HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request` for every other case

setup: the blame fixture plus bin.dat (contains NUL bytes), big.txt of 2,097,153 bytes and edge.txt of 2,097,152 bytes of text lines
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/blame_test.go, a table: {no path -> 400 invalid_request; path=nope -> 404 path_not_found; path=docs -> 400 invalid_request; path=bin.dat -> 400 invalid_request; path=big.txt (2 MiB + 1 byte) -> 413 payload_too_large; path=f.txt&start_line=0, start_line=5&end_line=4, start_line=7, start_line=x -> 400 invalid_request}: r = get('/scm/blame?' + q); assert (r.status, r.json.error.error_type) == want; assert get('/scm/blame?path=edge.txt').status == 200 for a file of exactly 2,097,152 bytes

requirements.title: Search
requirements.rationale: Finding where a string occurs at a ref should not need a checkout either.

criteria.condition: a caller requests `GET …/scm/search` with `q` of 1 to 500 characters
criteria.action: match `q` as a literal string, with regard to case, against the contents of every non-binary file at `ref` and return one `{path, line, text}` per matching line, ordered by path and then by line, with the resolved commit
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with `{items, next_cursor, resolved_sha}`; `line` is the 1-based line number and `text` the line without its line ending; characters of `q` that are special in regular expressions match themselves; a `q` that matches nothing answers `items: []`

setup: a fixture repository whose `main` holds api/greeting.go, docs/a.md, literal.txt containing the text `a.b(c)*`, and a binary file that contains the bytes of `Greeting`
check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/search_test.go: r = get('/scm/search?ref=main&q=Greeting'); assert r.json.items == [{path: 'api/greeting.go', line: 3, text: 'func Greeting() string {'}, {path: 'docs/a.md', line: 1, text: '# Greeting'}] and r.json.resolved_sha == head(main); assert get('/scm/search?q=greeting').json.items does not contain the 'Greeting' lines (case matters); assert paths of get('/scm/search?q=' + urlencode('a.b(c)*')) == ['literal.txt']; assert get('/scm/search?q=zzz-not-there').json == {items: [], next_cursor: null, resolved_sha: head}; and in internal/gitrepo/grep_test.go the same expectations against the grep function

criteria.condition: a search request carries `regex=true`, `case_sensitive=false` or `path`
criteria.action: with `regex=true` match `q` as an extended regular expression, with `case_sensitive=false` ignore case, and with `path` search only files whose path matches at least one glob
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the matching lines under the same ordering and shape

check.pseudocode: in internal/scm/search_test.go, a table over query -> expected (path, line) pairs: {q=func +[A-Z]\w*\(&regex=true -> the Go function lines; q=greeting&case_sensitive=false -> lines with 'Greeting' and 'greeting'; q=Greeting&path=docs/** -> only docs/a.md; q=Greeting&path=*.go&path=api/* -> only api/greeting.go; q=a.b&regex=true -> also lines where '.' stands for another character}

criteria.action: for any search, skip binary files and cut each match's `text` to its first 500 characters
criteria.contract: a file that git treats as binary yields no match even when it contains the bytes of `q`; a matching line of 2,000 characters is returned with a `text` of exactly 500 characters

setup: the search fixture plus long.txt with one line of 2,000 characters that starts with `needle`

requirements.title: Read commands of `parley scm`
requirements.rationale: A person or a script reaches the reads most often needed from the shell, with the output and exit codes every other command has.

criteria.condition: a user runs one of `parley scm refs|log|show|ls|diff|compare|blame|search` with its positional arguments and flags, and the hub answers 200
criteria.action: send one `GET` to the command's route under `/api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/scm` with each flag as the query parameter of the route, and print the response body
criteria.contract: stdout holds the response body as one JSON document and the exit status is 0; the request per command is: `refs <slug> --prefix P --limit N --cursor C` -> `/refs?prefix=P&limit=N&cursor=C`; `log <slug> --ref R --path P --follow --since S --until U --author A --stats --limit N --cursor C` -> `/commits` with `ref`, `path`, `follow=true`, `since`, `until`, `author`, `stats=true`, `limit`, `cursor`; `show <slug> <rev> --files` -> `/commits/<rev as one percent-encoded segment>?files=true`; `ls <slug> [path] --ref R --recursive` -> `/tree?path=…&ref=R&recursive=true`; `diff <slug> <base> <head> --mode M --path G…` -> `/diff?base=…&head=…&mode=M&path=G…`; `compare <slug> <base> <head>` -> `/compare?base=…&head=…`; `blame <slug> <path> --ref R --lines 3:9` -> `/blame?path=…&ref=R&start_line=3&end_line=9`; `search <slug> <query> --ref R --path G… --regex --ignore-case` -> `/search?q=…&ref=R&path=G…&regex=true&case_sensitive=false`; a flag that is not given sends no parameter

setup: an httptest server standing in for the hub; endpoint URL and credential given by flags
check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/scm_test.go, a table with one row per command line above plus each command with no flags: run the root command with the args against an httptest server that records the request and answers a canned JSON body; assert recorded method == GET, recorded path and recorded query (as a multimap) == want; assert stdout == the canned body indented by 2 spaces plus newline; assert exit == 0; rows include `show demo feature/x` -> escaped path '/api/v1/workspaces/demo/scm/commits/feature%2Fx' and `diff demo a b --path 'docs/**' --path '*.md'` -> two `path` values

criteria.condition: a user runs `parley scm cat <slug> <path>` with or without `--ref` and `--output <file>`, and the hub answers 200
criteria.action: request `GET …/scm/file?path=<path>` (with `ref` when given) without `Accept: application/json`, and write the body's raw bytes to stdout, or to the file when `--output` is given
criteria.contract: exit status 0; stdout holds exactly the file's bytes and no JSON framing; with `--output` stdout is empty and the named file holds exactly the bytes

check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/scm_test.go: the test hub answers bytes 0x00..0xff for /scm/file; run `scm cat demo bin.dat --ref v1`; assert recorded query == {path: bin.dat, ref: v1} and recorded Accept does not contain 'application/json'; assert stdout bytes == 0x00..0xff and exit == 0; out = t.TempDir()/f; run `scm cat demo bin.dat --output out`; assert stdout is empty and read(out) == the bytes

criteria.condition: `parley scm cat` receives an error answer from the hub, or cannot write the `--output` file
criteria.action: write no file content anywhere
criteria.contract: stdout is empty; no file is created at the `--output` path and an existing file there is left unchanged; for a hub error stderr holds the hub's error envelope and the exit status is 1; for a file that cannot be written stderr holds an envelope with `error_type` `client_error` and the exit status is 2

check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/scm_test.go: the test hub answers 404 path_not_found; out = t.TempDir()/f; run `scm cat demo nope --output out`; assert exit == 1 and stdout == '' and stderr json.error.error_type == 'path_not_found' and out does not exist; write 'keep' to out, run again; assert read(out) == 'keep'; with the hub answering 200: run `scm cat demo f --output <t.TempDir()>/missing-dir/f`; assert exit == 2 and stderr json.error.error_type == 'client_error'

criteria.condition: a user runs `parley scm diff` with `--patch` or with `--name-only`
criteria.action: with `--patch` request `format=patch` and print the unified diff text as received; with `--name-only` request `patches=false` and print the JSON response
criteria.contract: exit status 0; with `--patch` stdout is the response's text byte for byte, not JSON; with `--name-only` stdout is the JSON document, whose files carry no patch text

check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/scm_test.go: the test hub answers 'diff --git a/x b/x\n…' with Content-Type text/x-diff when format=patch; run `scm diff demo main feature --patch`; assert recorded query has format=patch and stdout == the text exactly; run `scm diff demo main feature --name-only`; assert recorded query has patches=false and no format, and stdout parses as the canned JSON

criteria.condition: a user runs `parley scm compare <slug> <base> <head> --fail-on-conflict` and the hub's answer has `mergeable` equal to `conflict`
criteria.action: print the response and report that the requested condition was not met
criteria.contract: stdout holds the response body as one JSON document; stderr holds an envelope with `code` 0 and `error_type` `condition_not_met`; the exit status is 3; with `mergeable` `clean`, or without the flag, the exit status is 0 and stderr is empty

check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/scm_test.go, a table over (mergeable, flag) -> exit: {(conflict, --fail-on-conflict) -> 3; (clean, --fail-on-conflict) -> 0; (conflict, no flag) -> 0}: run `scm compare demo main feature` with the row's flag against a test hub answering the row's body; assert exit == want; assert stdout parses to the canned body in every row; for the first row assert stderr json.error == {code: 0, error_type: 'condition_not_met', message: non-empty}

criteria.condition: a `parley scm` read command is run with the wrong number of positional arguments, with `--mode` other than `merge_base` or `direct`, with `--patch` together with `--name-only`, with a `--lines` value that is not `<start>:<end>` with two positive integers, or with a `--limit` that is not an integer
criteria.action: fail before sending any request
criteria.contract: stdout is empty; stderr holds an envelope with `code` 0 and `error_type` `usage_error`; the exit status is 2; the hub receives no request

check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/scm_test.go, a table over args = {scm refs; scm show demo; scm cat demo; scm diff demo main; scm compare demo a b c; scm diff demo a b --mode sideways; scm diff demo a b --patch --name-only; scm blame demo f --lines 3; scm blame demo f --lines a:b; scm blame demo f --lines 0:2; scm refs demo --limit many}: run against a test hub that counts requests; assert exit == 2 and stdout == '' and stderr json.error.error_type == 'usage_error' and hub.requests == 0

steps.action: sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo/scm/file?ref=main&path=README.md with a PAT that holds git:read

authenticates the PAT, checks the scope and the workspace access, resolves `main` to its head commit and answers the file's bytes with X-Parley-Resolved-Sha, an ETag and Cache-Control private, no-cache
repeats the request with If-None-Match set to the ETag, then with ref set to the 40-character id from X-Parley-Resolved-Sha
answers 304 to the first, and to the second the same bytes with Cache-Control private, max-age=31536000, immutable
sends GET …/scm/diff with base and head set to two commit ids taken from GET …/scm/commits
answers the file changes between the two commits with their patch text and reports each read to the request recorder

setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its data directory in t.TempDir()
workspace `demo` in status ready whose repository holds two commits on `main`, the second changing README.md, registered the way the end-to-end tests of package 10 register a workspace

end_state: the first read answered 200 with the bytes of README.md at the head of main

execution_paths.title: A review agent asks from the shell whether a branch still applies and gets the conflict as data

steps.action: runs `parley scm compare demo main feature --fail-on-conflict`
sends GET /api/v1/workspaces/demo/scm/compare?base=main&head=feature with the configured credential

resolves both revisions, counts ahead and behind, runs a trial rebase of feature onto main that stops at a conflicting commit, and answers 200 with mergeable conflict and the conflict report, moving no ref
prints the response on stdout, reports condition_not_met on stderr and exits 3
runs `parley scm cat demo f.txt --ref main` to read the target's side of the conflicted file
answers the raw bytes of f.txt at the head of main, which the CLI writes to stdout

the parleyd HTTP server and its authentication, scope and access checks
the scm read routes of internal/scm
the trial rebase of internal/gitrepo running the real git binary on a bare repository on disk
setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its data directory in t.TempDir()
workspace `demo` in status ready with branches `main` and `feature` that both changed the same line of f.txt after their merge base
the CLI configured with the hub's URL and the API key of the workspace's owner through PARLEY_ENDPOINT_URL and PARLEY_API_KEY
end_state: its stdout is one JSON document with mergeable conflict and a conflict report naming f.txt with kind content
its stderr holds an envelope with error_type condition_not_met
